dct_description_sm: The High Arctic is characterized by many extreme climatic and geomorphologic phenomena. According to the last climatic scenarios, climate changes will affect the Arctic more than any other region of the planet. The High Arctic, which is essentially bare of vegetation, will have a strong response to climate changes and will be marked by an acceleration of periglacial processes associated with permafrost thawing. Mass movements will be favored by the deepening of the active layer which will supply more water to favor the creeping and the continuous sliding of the material over the ice-rich permafrost table. The project focuses on the influence of solifluction lobes' movement on the permafrost dynamic at Ward Hunt Island, Nunavut (Canada). The hydrologic budget of Ward Hunt Island lies essentially on the incoming water from snowmelt and from active layer hydrogeology during the short annual thawing period. On the island, many solifluction lobes deform sediments and drive mass movement downslope. Considering the recent deepening of the active layer, the higher incoming material downslope may modify ground ice aggradation and permafrost dynamics. This dynamic is not yet considered by permafrost modeling scenarios.
dct_title_s: Mass movement by solifluction and syngenetic dynamic of permafrost in the High Arctic, Canadian High Arctic
